title: Disability Insurance: The Coverage Most People Skip (and Shouldn't)
metaDescription: Most people insure their car and home but skip insuring their income. Here's why disability insurance matters and how to think about it.
bodyHtml:
You probably insure your car. You probably insure your home or your apartment's contents. If you have kids or a spouse who depends on your income, you may already have life insurance. But there's one asset most people never insure at all: their ability to earn a paycheck.

That's what disability insurance is for. It replaces part of your income if an illness or injury keeps you from working. It's one of the least glamorous products in personal finance, which is probably why so many people skip it. But the math on how often it's actually needed is worth a second look.

The odds are higher than most people assume

Disability feels like something that happens to other people, usually after a dramatic accident. In reality, most long-term disabilities come from ordinary health problems: back injuries, heart conditions, cancer, mental health conditions, and other chronic illnesses that build up over time.

The Social Security Administration puts real numbers behind this. A 20-year-old worker has a 1-in-4 chance of developing a disability before reaching full retirement age.
